# 菩薩睒子經

**ID:** T0174
**Volume:** T03
**Category:** 本緣部類
**Original Category:** 本緣部
**Byline:** 失譯
**Date:** 265–316
**Juans:** 1
**CBETA:** https://cbetaonline.dila.edu.tw/zh/T0174

## Summary (Ask Bunkankun 聞分館君)

A short single-fascicle *jātaka* recounting the past life of the Buddha as the Bodhisattva *Śyāmaka* (睒子), the perfectly filial son who served his blind ascetic parents in the forest, and was killed by mistake by King Pīluō (毘羅勒 in this recension) hunting deer; the gods restored his life on account of his filial virtue. Signature: 「安公錄中闕譯今附西晉錄」 ("[Dào]ān's catalog records this as a missing-translator [text]; presently appended to the Western-Jìn register").

The *Śyāmaka-jātaka* is one of the most widely-attested *jātaka*s, paralleled in the Pāli *Sāma-jātaka* (no. 540), the *Mahāvastu*, and across Asian Buddhist art (Bharhut, Sānchī, Ajaṇṭā, and Dūnhuáng).

**Abstract**

T174 is the canonical anonymous-translator version of the Chinese *Śyāmaka-jātaka*, paralleled by [聖堅](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E8%81%96%E5%A0%85) Shèngjiān's three Western-Qín translations [T175a](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0027), [T175b](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0028), and [T175c](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0029) (the same translation transmitted in three slightly different recensions). The Western-Jìn register-attribution is by [道安](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E9%81%93%E5%AE%89) Dào'ān's catalog (preserved in [僧祐](https://ask.bunkankun.org/Persons/%E5%83%A7%E7%A5%90) Sēngyòu); modern scholarship places the actual translation in roughly the same period (late third / early fourth century).

The narrative was foundational in the East-Asian Buddhist accommodation of filial-piety ethics: alongside *[T167 Tàizǐ Mùpò jīng](https://ask.bunkankun.org/KR6/KR6b/KR6b0019)* and the parallels to *Sudāna* / *Vessantara*, the *Śyāmaka*-narrative was one of the principal Buddhist *exempla* read by medieval Chinese Buddhist exegetes as evidence that *bodhisattva*-virtue and Confucian filial-piety converge.
